questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Good courses and an in teresting destination

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy to ask questions and get quick and good answers

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Study Abroad hosted some informal meetings

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Not easy in London. But I found the Danish Hostel, which is easy to get a spot at as a dane.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is difficult to meet people unless you live at the Danish Hostel. On this type of hostel social relations were a given.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was frustrating that Housing were only available for American students on Study Abroad

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to make an account on the QM mail and the QM-Plus which was confusing but you'll get the hang of it

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I could always contact the people on Study Abroad and get a quick and friendly answer

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Succesful – I got the courses I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask as many questions as you need. And it is always confusing in the beginning.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had four courses which was a lot

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At QMUL the teaching were more about learning how to form a good argument and take a stand to what we read and discussed. At UCPH the teaching is more focused on learning us all the different ways to which you can look at a subject and all the different theories there is on a specific topic, and teaching us to be able to reflect on different theories and ways of looking at a specific topic – so our discussions are more objective.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Race in America, Consumerism in America, The American Century, The Soviet Union

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Race in America was my all-time favorite course. It is really interesting and eyeopening, and the texts we read was interesting and gave new perspectives. Would recommend this course to all.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Transportation was unexpectedly expensive. I had to pay for an expensive cover-test as well. I took the express train from the airport into London, which I didn't know would cost me £22 aside from my day-ticket for busses and the under- and overground.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The rent was surprisingly cheap at the Danish House. Still I had to sleep with three other girls.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You could participate in the different societies and the University. But really, I didn't have the time when my courses were different from what I'm used too and therefor really comprehensive for me. So the social life on my University was pretty limiting. There wasn't any including, get-to-know-each-other activities on my courses, so I didn't really get to know any of the people I were studying with, which was a pity.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go on dates. Also just friendly dates. If you have the time participate in a society that interests you. There were several danish activities at through the Danish Hostel where you could meet other Danes, which was fun.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: See the different areas of the city – in London go to the different cinemas (and get some memberships!) and the different museums that interests you, get a Sunday roast, find the good pubs in your area and go to concerts or festivals. Explore on your own but make some appointments with friends or dates in the evenings as well. Also get there before the study starts so you have some time to explore.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Try and find them in the cafe and talk and maybe ask for their instagrams so you can contact them and maybe hang out.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Mostly I found it hard to adjust to the way they study. How to write an essay and an learning log when you've never done one.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their friendliness, courtesy and casual way of converse with strangers. How they're so talkative and funny.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Move into the Danish Hostel if you want to have a social community while you're there. But also make sure to get out of the hostel and explore the city in your own way. Don't use all your time on school. Challenge yourself

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Dating and studying

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
